evidence_quality: Each candidate has a mathematically typed preliminary definition and mathematical source or qualified source lead. Sources marked lead require exact verification before provisional staging; URLs alone are not proof of correctness.

high_priority_review_flags.issue: Lebesgue-Stieltjes measure convention requires right-continuity of distribution function for the interval (a,b] assignment; mere monotonicity insufficient.
Residue-field inclusion Λ/(Λ∩m)→R/m need not be surjective without an explicit assumption; do not call it an isomorphism automatically.
Braiding needs hexagon coherence, not only natural exchange isomorphisms.
Division ring/field formulation may require 1≠0 rather than vacuous zero-ring interpretation.

items.original_context: Real vector space: weighted Minkowski set sum tC+(1−t)C={tx+(1−t)y:x,y∈C}, with the two elements selected independently.
items.definition_paraphrase: For C⊆V and scalar t∈R, the Minkowski set sum tC+(1−t)C is {tx+(1−t)y:x,y∈C}.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: The two choices x and y are independent. For 0≤t≤1, convexity of C is equivalent to tC+(1−t)C⊆C for all such t; for t outside this interval the same set exists but not a convex combination.

items.original_query: prime ideals minimal over its annihilator Ann_R(m)
items.original_context: Commutative algebra: prime ideal p minimal over an ideal I in a commutative unital ring R, meaning I⊆p and no prime ideal q satisfies I⊆q⊊p; the ideal here is Ann_R(m) for a module element m.
items.definition_paraphrase: A prime ideal p is minimal over an ideal I⊆R when I⊆p and no prime q satisfies I⊆q⊊p.

sources.section: Existence of minimal primes over ideals
sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: Annihilator Ann_R(m) is a specific choice of I. Minimal over I differs from minimal prime of R unless I=0.

items.original_query: Cat as category of small categories
items.original_context: Category theory: category Cat with small categories as objects, functors as morphisms, and functor composition; set-theoretic universe issues must be handled explicitly.
items.definition_paraphrase: The category Cat has small categories as objects and functors as its morphisms, composed as ordinary functors; the surrounding universe/category size must be specified.

sources.section: Remark 4.2.2 on small and big categories
sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: Cat is generally large relative to the universe containing its small categories; do not identify it with the category of all unrestricted large categories.

items.original_query: kernel of automorphism mapping F on an object
items.original_context: Category theory: kernel of the induced group homomorphism Aut_S(x)→Aut_{S′}(F(x)) given by a functor F of categories fibred over C, comprising automorphisms α of x with F(α)=id_{F(x)}; the arrows should be vertical when defining relative inertia over C.
items.definition_paraphrase: For an induced group map Aut_S(x)→Aut_{S′}(F(x)), its kernel consists of the automorphisms α of x mapped to the identity automorphism of F(x).

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: Relative inertia over base C restricts to vertical automorphisms p(α)=id; general Aut_S(x) need not consist only of vertical automorphisms.

items.original_context: Restriction f|_U:U→M of map f:X→M to U⊆X, retaining the original values.
items.definition_paraphrase: For f:X→Y and U⊆X, the restriction f|_U:U→Y sends u↦f(u).

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: No extension or recomputation of values. The codomain remains Y unless explicitly co-restricted to an image subspace.

items.original_context: Measure theory: nonnegative Lebesgue–Stieltjes measure generated by admissible bounded nondecreasing function on real line, respecting its measure convention.
items.definition_paraphrase: A Lebesgue–Stieltjes measure from a monotone function F is a Borel measure assigning μ((a,b])=F(b)−F(a), when F satisfies the required right-continuity/measure-construction conventions.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: Mere nondecreasing bounded F is not enough for the usual (a,b] convention: if F has a right-discontinuity, the interval assignment fails countable additivity. Replace by an appropriate right-continuous representative or use an alternative interval convention.

items.original_query: automorphism α of x over identity of p(x)
items.original_context: Category theory of fibred categories: a vertical automorphism α:x→x in a category S over C, invertible in S and satisfying p(α)=id_{p(x)} in C. The base identity condition is part of verticality, not automatic for a general endomorphism of S.
items.definition_paraphrase: A vertical automorphism of x over C is an invertible arrow α:x→x in S such that p(α)=id_{p(x)}.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: A general automorphism of x may project to nonidentity automorphism of p(x). The kernel-group condition belongs to a separate construction.

items.original_context: Measure theory: μ-integrability of x↦x^n means measurability and ∫_{(a,b)}|x|^n dμ(x)<∞, for n a nonnegative integer, under the conventional finite-L1 meaning of integrable.
items.definition_paraphrase: For measurable x↦x^n, μ-integrability means ∫|x|^n dμ<∞ for n≥0, measured on the stated domain.

sources.section: Finite integral and support in measure-theoretic applications
sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: At n=0 the integrand is conventionally 1 and integrability becomes finite total measure; 0^0 must not be handled by arbitrary pointwise exponent conventions.

items.original_context: Metric topology: topology τ_d generated by all open metric balls as a basis, on the same underlying set X of metric d.
items.definition_paraphrase: For metric space (X,d), τ_d consists of subsets U⊆X such that for each x∈U there exists ε>0 with B_d(x,ε)⊆U.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: The empty set and X are open; metric balls generate τ_d as a basis, and the underlying set is the same X.

items.original_context: Real analysis: bounded function on a fixed compact interval [a,b], meaning there exists M≥0 with |f(x)|≤M for all x in [a,b].
items.definition_paraphrase: For f:[a,b]→R, boundedness means ∃M≥0 such that |f(x)|≤M for all x∈[a,b].

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: Compactness alone does not make an arbitrary function bounded; continuity on the compact interval would imply boundedness.

items.original_context: Complex linear algebra: Hermitian sesquilinear form on complex vector space V, linear in first argument, conjugate linear in second and conjugate symmetric.
items.definition_paraphrase: A Hermitian sesquilinear form h:V×V→C is linear in its first argument, conjugate linear in its second and satisfies h(y,x)=conj(h(x,y)).

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: Some sources choose linearity in second argument; preserve selected convention consistently. Positive definiteness is not part of Hermitian sesquilinear form.

items.original_context: Graded algebra: degree-zero component of the localized graded ring S_f, closed under ring operations, with homogeneous fractions a/f^n satisfying deg(a)=n deg(f).
items.definition_paraphrase: For graded ring S=⊕_{d∈Z}S_d, the degree-zero subring S_0 consists of homogeneous degree-zero elements; for homogeneous f, (S_f)_0 consists of a/f^n with deg(a)=n·deg(f).

sources.section: Proj of graded rings and degree-zero localizations
sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: If f has positive degree, numerators are homogeneous of the specified matching degree. Arbitrary sum of nonhomogeneous numerators can be rewritten but needs correct grading.

items.original_context: Category and module theory: natural isomorphism of covariant functors in the target S-module N between Hom_S(P,N) and the sets of R-linear differential operators Diff^k_{S/R}(M,N), with components commuting with postcomposition along every S-linear map N→N′.
items.definition_paraphrase: A natural identification Hom_S(P,N)≅Diff^k_{S/R}(M,N) consists of bijections η_N natural in the S-module N, meaning η_{N′}(u∘h)=u∘η_N(h) for every S-linear u:N→N′.

sources.section: Modules of principal parts and representability of differential operators
sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: Do not confuse natural isomorphism of functors with a single set bijection. Existence of representing module P is a separate theorem requiring stated hypotheses.

items.original_context: Commutative algebra: radical ideal of a commutative ring
items.definition_paraphrase: An ideal I in a commutative ring R is radical if whenever r^n∈I for an integer n≥1, then r∈I; equivalently I=√I.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: The radical √I is an ideal. Every prime ideal is radical but not every radical ideal is prime.

items.original_context: Multilinear algebra: induced R-linear map ∧^rφ:∧^rR^m→∧^rR^n obtained by applying φ to each factor before exterior multiplication.
items.definition_paraphrase: For R-linear φ:M→N, the induced exterior-power map ∧^rφ:∧^rM→∧^rN is determined by v_1∧⋯∧v_r↦φ(v_1)∧⋯∧φ(v_r).

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: r≥0. For r=0 it is the identity on R under the usual ∧^0M=R convention. It does not require φ invertible.

items.original_context: Orthogonal-polynomial analysis: finiteness of every nonnegative integer weighted absolute moment Σ_{x∈X}|x|^k w_x over a countably supported positive weight.
items.definition_paraphrase: For weights w_x>0 on countable support X, finiteness of every absolute moment means Σ_{x∈X}|x|^k w_x<∞ for all k∈N_0.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: At k=0 this imposes Σ w_x<∞ (finite total mass), not merely positivity of individual weights. All summands are nonnegative, so convergence is unambiguous as a supremum of finite subsums.

items.original_context: Category theory: pro-object of category C, a formal cofiltered inverse diagram representing a formal inverse limit in Pro(C), not necessarily an actual limit in C.
items.definition_paraphrase: A pro-object of C can be represented by a functor I→C indexed by a small cofiltered category I, formally specifying an object in Pro(C), with morphisms defined by appropriate lim-colim formula.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: An actual inverse limit of the diagram in C need not exist. Specify index-size conditions and equivalence of pro-diagrams under the chosen foundation.

items.original_context: Group theory: restriction of ambient binary operation ⋆:G×G→G to H×H, where H is closed under that operation and the restriction maps into H.
items.definition_paraphrase: Given H⊆G closed under ⋆, the ambient group operation restricts to H×H→H via (x,y)↦x⋆y.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: Closure under multiplication alone need not make H a subgroup; identity and inverses also required.

items.original_context: Linear algebra: image of a K-linear transformation as a subspace of target W admitting a finite K-basis.
items.definition_paraphrase: For K-linear T:V→W, im(T)={T(v):v∈V} is a K-vector subspace of W; it is finite-dimensional if it admits a finite basis.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: Finite dimension of im(T) is an added condition: it need not follow from T linear when V infinite-dimensional.

items.original_context: Topology: diagonal subset Δ_X consisting of equal-coordinate ordered pairs in X×X.
items.definition_paraphrase: For any set X, its diagonal is Δ_X={(x,x):x∈X}⊆X×X.

sources.section: Topological diagonal and closed points in separation discussions
sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: For X=∅, Δ_X=∅. The diagonal is closed in X×X iff X is Hausdorff; do not include closedness as part of the definition.

items.original_context: Set theory: singleton set {a} and unordered doubleton {a,b} used as finite set constructors in the Kuratowski pair {{a},{a,b}}; distinguish singleton from unordered pair in later missing-meaning research.
items.definition_paraphrase: A singleton {a} has exactly element a, and an unordered pair {a,b} consists of the elements equal to a or b. The Kuratowski ordered pair is (a,b):={{a},{a,b}}.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: If a=b then {a,b}={a}. The Kuratowski encoding still distinguishes ordered pairs through outer nested sets, not by treating {a,b} itself as ordered.

items.original_context: Order theory: least element a∈A of a subset A of a partially ordered set, such that a≤x for every x∈A; unlike a merely minimal element.
items.definition_paraphrase: A least element a of subset A in poset (P,≤) is an element a∈A with a≤x for every x∈A.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: Least element is unique by antisymmetry; a merely minimal element need not be comparable to every other element.

items.original_context: Homological algebra: cochain complex induced by contravariant Hom_R(−,N) on a chain complex F_•, with coboundary maps induced by precomposition with the original differentials.
items.definition_paraphrase: For a chain complex F_• and R-module N, Hom_R(F_•,N) is a cochain complex with cochains Hom_R(F_n,N) and differential δ^n(h)=h∘d_{n+1}.

sources.section: Hom complex and cohomology of complexes
sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: Variance reverses arrows. Some authors include signs in total complexes, but for this simple Hom into degree-zero N the precomposition formula is standard.

items.original_context: Real analysis: Riemann sum associated to a bounded real-valued function and a tagged finite partition; sum of f(ξ_i)(x_i−x_{i−1}).
items.definition_paraphrase: Given tagged partition a=x_0<⋯<x_n=b with ξ_i∈[x_{i−1},x_i], the Riemann sum is Σ_{i=1}^n f(ξ_i)(x_i−x_{i−1}).

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: No convergence assumption needed to define one sum. A Riemann integral exists when tagged sums converge in the required mesh sense.

items.original_context: Sheaf theory: morphism from inverse-image sheaf f^{-1}O_Y on X to O_X, adjoint to O_Y→f_*O_X; not an ordinary preimage of subsets.
items.definition_paraphrase: For continuous f:X→Y, a morphism f^{-1}O_Y→O_X of sheaves of rings on X is adjoint to O_Y→f_*O_X, by inverse-image/pushforward adjunction.

sources.section: Morphisms of ringed spaces and adjoint sheaf map
sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: Inverse-image sheaf f^{-1}O_Y is a sheaf construction, not set-theoretic preimage f^{-1}(B). For locally ringed spaces additional stalk-locality required.

items.original_context: Graded algebra: irrelevant ideal S_+=⊕_{n>0} S_n, generated by positive-degree homogeneous elements of a nonnegatively graded ring.
items.definition_paraphrase: For a nonnegatively graded ring S=⊕_{n≥0}S_n, the irrelevant ideal is S_+=⊕_{n>0}S_n.

sources.section: Irrelevant ideal in Proj of graded rings
sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: If grading has negative degrees, positive-degree sum need not be an ideal without extra grading conventions. Here nonnegative grading is required.

items.original_context: Category theory: natural braiding or symmetry c_{X,Y}:X⊗Y→Y⊗X in monoidal category, natural in X,Y; for symmetric structure the double exchange is the identity.
items.definition_paraphrase: A braiding in monoidal C consists of natural isomorphisms c_{X,Y}:X⊗Y→Y⊗X satisfying hexagon axioms; symmetry requires c_{Y,X}∘c_{X,Y}=id.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: A family of arbitrary 'exchange' maps alone is not a braiding; coherence axioms matter. No automatic symmetry unless double exchange identity specified.

items.original_context: Integer arithmetic: product on natural-number difference classes given by [(a,b)]·[(c,d)]=[(ac+bd,ad+bc)], requiring well-definedness on equivalence classes and yielding a distributive unital ring operation.
items.definition_paraphrase: On equivalence classes of pairs (a,b) of natural numbers modeling a−b, multiplication is [(a,b)]·[(c,d)]=[(ac+bd,ad+bc)].

sources.section: Integers via equivalence classes of natural pairs
sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: Well-definedness modulo (a,b)∼(a′,b′) iff a+b′=a′+b must be proved; one formula alone is not a ring construction.

items.original_context: Commutative algebra and order theory: saturated finite strict chain of primes p=p_0⊊p_1⊊⋯⊊p_n=q between fixed p⊆q, with no prime strictly between adjacent terms; maximal under refinement, not necessarily of greatest length.
items.definition_paraphrase: A finite saturated chain between prime ideals p⊆q is p=p_0⊊⋯⊊p_n=q where no prime lies strictly between adjacent p_i,p_{i+1}.

sources.section: Catenary rings and maximal saturated chains
sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: Saturated/maximal-by-refinement chain need not have maximum length in a noncatenary ring. Require existence of finite chain separately.

items.original_context: Algebra: n-fold repeated addition of multiplicative identity 1_F in the additive abelian group of a field F, for positive integer n.
items.definition_paraphrase: For n∈N, n·1_F is the sum of n copies of the field unit 1_F in the additive group of F; 0·1_F=0_F.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: In positive characteristic, n·1_F may be zero for n>0; this is not multiplication of two formal natural integers inside F without canonical map.

items.original_context: Commutative local algebra: field isomorphism Λ/(Λ∩m)→R/m induced by inclusion Λ⊆R, preserving the chosen maps and residue-field structures.
items.definition_paraphrase: A ring inclusion Λ⊆R induces Λ/(Λ∩m)→R/m for ideal m of R. It is an isomorphism precisely when the induced residue map is both injective and surjective.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: Injectivity into R/m is automatic with kernel Λ∩m, but surjectivity is NOT automatic; do not claim an isomorphism without this added hypothesis. Λ∩m must be maximal to call source quotient a field.

items.original_query: multiplicative group F× of field units
items.original_context: Field and group theory: F×=F\{0} with group operation given by field multiplication, identity 1_F and multiplicative inverse of each nonzero element. This is the unit group of the field, distinct from the ambient additive group.
items.definition_paraphrase: For a field F, its multiplicative group of units F×=F\{0} with field multiplication and identity 1_F.

sources.section: Nonzero field elements form multiplicative group
sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: F× differs from additive group (F,+). Zero element is excluded; every remaining element invertible.

items.original_context: Category theory: two-sided Ore completion properties for arrows in a category localized at S, involving commutative squares for eligible cospans and spans.
items.definition_paraphrase: Left and right Ore-square completion properties specify completion of eligible spans/cospans involving chosen denominators in S to commutative diagrams in a localization calculus.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: The exact left/right orientations are source-convention dependent. Do not falsely replace with a statement that arbitrary squares can be completed.

items.original_context: Algebra: polynomial P(T) in the univariate polynomial algebra ℚ[T], evaluated at sufficiently large nonnegative integer n, with rational coefficients and finite degree.
items.definition_paraphrase: For P(T)=Σ_{i=0}^d a_i T^i∈Q[T], evaluation at n∈Z is P(n)=Σ_{i=0}^d a_i n^i∈Q.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: The qualifier 'sufficiently large n' applies to a property under study, not the existence of evaluation, which is defined for every integer n.

items.original_context: Set theory and commutative algebra: intersection ∩_{j∈J}I_j of an indexed family of ideals of a unital ring R, the elements belonging to every I_j; the empty-family intersection is R.
items.definition_paraphrase: The intersection of a family (I_j)_{j∈J} of ideals is {r∈R: r∈I_j for every j∈J}, itself an ideal; empty-family intersection equals R.

sources.section: Rings and ideals; intersection as subobject
sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: Intersection of all maximal ideals is the Jacobson radical of R, with unit-ring conventions; not the same as nilradical in general.

items.original_context: Set theory: union ⋃_{i∈I}U_i of a possibly infinite indexed family of subsets of X, including empty-index union ∅; the requirement that this union belong to τ is an axiom defining a topology.
items.definition_paraphrase: For subsets U_i⊆X, the indexed union ⋃_{i∈I}U_i is {x∈X:∃i∈I,x∈U_i}.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: When I=∅ the union is ∅. Every topology is closed under all such unions.

items.original_query: every nonzero element has two-sided inverse
items.original_context: Ring theory: two-sided multiplicative inverse b for an element a≠0 in a unital ring, satisfying ab=ba=1_D; stronger than a one-sided inverse.
items.definition_paraphrase: For a nonzero element a in a unital ring D, b is a two-sided multiplicative inverse if ab=ba=1_D.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: For division rings every nonzero element has an inverse; commutativity is additionally needed to be a field. The zero ring needs a nontriviality convention to avoid vacuous division-ring claims.

items.original_context: Commutative algebra: radical sqrt(I)={r∈R:r^n∈I for some positive integer n} of an ideal I in a commutative ring R.
items.definition_paraphrase: For ideal I⊆R in a commutative ring, √I={r∈R: r^n∈I for some n≥1}.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: I radical iff I=√I. Do not equate √I with the intersection of only maximal ideals containing I; in general use all prime ideals.

items.original_context: Set theory: two sets A and B are equipotent (equinumerous) exactly when a bijection A→B exists; this is a relation between sets, not the witnessing bijective function itself.
items.definition_paraphrase: Sets A and B are equipotent when there exists a bijective function f:A→B.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: Equipotence relates sets; the witnessing bijection itself is a different mathematical object.

items.original_context: General topology: closed point x of a topological space X, meaning the singleton {x} is closed as a subset of X (not merely relatively closed in a closed subset Z⊆X).
items.definition_paraphrase: A point x∈X is closed when the singleton {x} is closed in X.

sources.relevance: Evidence of definition or contextual mathematical lead; see scope and verification status, not automatically certified.

items.mathematical_edge_case_or_comparison: Closedness is relative to ambient X, not just a subspace. Every point is closed iff X is T1; the empty space has no points.
